name: Mauritania
summary_text: Mauritania is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely — one of the world's most dangerous legal environments. The 1983 Penal Code criminalises “acts against nature” with death by stoning (de facto moratorium on executions, but the statute is live); and Cairo 52 documents that gender nonconformity is effectively criminalised through debauchery, heresy, and Islamic-morality provisions — trans people can be apprehended solely for their gender expression. There is no LGR, no healthcare, no community, and sharia courts operate alongside the civil system.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents that Mauritania criminalises same-sex sexual activity with a possible death penalty under Sharia law.

sources.title: Mauritania | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Mauritania: gender nonconformity is effectively criminalised through 'debauchery', 'heresy' and anti-Sharia provisions - trans people can be apprehended solely for their identity and expression; no gender-affirming healthcare; no legal recognition framework (legislation grounded in Sharia precludes transition); grave lack of information on the trans community.

sources.title: Mauritania - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2023 Human Rights Report for Mauritania: official assessment - same-sex conduct punishable by death under Sharia-based law; significant societal stigma; no recent executions reported.

sources.title: Spotlight on Mauritania, where LGBT people hide their identities for fear of stigma
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (Jan 2026), based on Outright International's country overview: the Penal Code provides a maximum sentence of death by stoning for men; the government confirmed a de facto moratorium in 2021; arrests, detentions and harassment reported; low visibility fuels stigma; Mauritania became a refuge for some Senegalese LGBTIQ people after 2008.

sources.title: Liberals Network of Mauritania – voice of free people
sources.claim_summary: Liberals Mauritania (founded 2014): 'the voice of the freethinkers in Mauritania' - mission to combat mistreatment and prejudice towards non-believers and LGBTQ individuals, eradicate systemic discrimination; publishes on the criminalisation law, apostasy/blasphemy laws, and the story of the first trans woman in Mauritanian media.
